supersedes: compatibility/fixtures/mcp/hieronymus_rag_search/wire.success.json :: the FTS-only success (a lexical-only answer is no longer a valid hieronymus_rag_search result)
rule: Versioned Rust expectation, separate from the frozen Python fixtures (whose bytes stay unchanged). Review finding A5: the Rust hieronymus_rag_search ran hieronymus::rag::RagStore::search directly — a lexical FTS query that neither consumed the semantic lane nor required readiness — so a missing, unconfigured, acquiring, rebuilding, or failed semantic runtime produced an ordinary successful result array and no caller could tell that the semantic half never ran. Both working memory and semantic RAG are mandatory (M2/S2 completion contract): FTS-only is not a completion or release alternative, and a temporarily degraded semantic service must report its limits rather than serve the lexical half as if it were complete. The tool now (a) gates on the shared semantic-availability signal — the daemon's semantic controller state through require_semantic_ready — and (b) serves hieronymus::recall::RecallService::search_series, the same armed semantic lane plus reciprocal-rank fusion that hieronymus_recall runs, as a session-less series+query search with no synthetic task session. THE ENVELOPE AND ROW SHAPE ARE UNCHANGED: the response is still the bare array of row objects the frozen outputSchema describes, with the same keys, so no consumer has to be rewritten. Two things change. (1) Availability: a semantic service that is absent (no daemon owns the application), acquiring, rebuilding, or failed makes the call a tool error carrying the service's own actionable reason, where it previously returned lexical rows. A ready service over a series with no indexed chunks is an empty success (ready-for-ingest), never an error; a ready service whose lane then cannot execute over a series that HAS chunks is an error, because the alternative is a lexical-only answer dressed up as a complete one. (2) Score semantics: rows are the fused hybrid result, so score is the reciprocal-rank-fusion score over the FTS and semantic lanes (RRF k=60, ranks only, never raw lane scores) rather than the raw FTS score, and rank_reason distinguishes the lanes — a chunk the FTS lane carried keeps its lexical reason (e.g. 'rag project text match'), while a chunk only the semantic lane surfaced carries 'rag semantic match'. Mixed hieronymus_recall keeps its recall-v2 DTO and never hard-fails on missing semantics — memory and deterministic terminology still serve — but its warnings now carry semantic_lane_unavailable whenever required semantics did not run over the current corpus, including the unarmed lane that recall-v2 previously recorded as silent. ADR 0013 governs semantic-index identity, series isolation, and generation discipline, all of which this delta preserves (series filtering happens inside the ANN query, generations are never mixed); the mandatory-semantics half of the rule is the owner's M2/S2 completion contract, not a claim about ADR 0013's FTS5-only release baseline, which concerns what a RELEASE may ship, not what a tool advertised as semantic RAG search may silently answer.

envelope.note: No {results, semantic} wrapper was introduced: with the availability gate ahead of retrieval there is no partial-success path left to describe on the success side, and the frozen outputSchema (hieronymus_rag_searchOutput: {result: array of objects}) keeps describing the payload exactly.
